name: flight-duty
title: Pilot flight, duty and rest limits under FAA rules
summary: Check a pilot's schedule against the US FAA's flight and duty limits: flight time, duty periods, augmented crews, time zones, split duty, extensions, reserve, rest and night flying.
description: Each task gives an unnamed pilot's facts: where the pilot is acclimated, report time, flight legs and block times, the crew and its rest facility, earlier duty and rest, every time with its date and UTC offset. The AI reads the FAA's flight and duty limits for flightcrew members, 14 CFR Part 117, with its Tables A, B and C, and answers what they decide, mostly to the minute: the limit that applies, how much is used and left, or whether a schedule is allowed. Every field of the answer is checked, and a task passes only when all of them are right.

families.name: Flight time
families.what: The maximum flight time of Table A against scheduled and actual block times, with deadhead legs that count for none.

families.name: Flight duty period
families.what: The flight duty period limit of Table B: where the period starts and ends, which legs count and across time zones.

families.name: Augmented crews
families.what: The limit of Table C by rest facility class and number of pilots, with the flight time and segment limits of an augmented crew.

families.name: Acclimation
families.what: Whether a pilot is acclimated in a new theater, and the limit that follows.

families.name: Split duty
families.what: Whether a rest during the duty period meets every condition of split duty, and what it does to the limit.

families.name: Extensions
families.what: How far a flight duty period may be extended, how often, and when the extension must be reported.

families.name: Reserve duty
families.what: The limits of airport or standby, short-call and long-call reserve.

families.name: Cumulative limits
families.what: Flight time and flight duty period hours in the consecutive hours or calendar days that end at a given moment.

families.name: Rest
families.what: The rest required before a report, in the past 168 hours, after a long trip and after a deadhead.

families.name: Night operations
families.what: Which flight duty periods infringe on the window of circadian low, and how many may follow in a row.
